actual_cues.text: From Settings, open Active Unit and choose the apparatus whose
inventory you intend to check.
Select Unit lists the available vehicles; this fictional fire and
EMS example uses Ambulance 61.
Read the selected unit name again in the sidebar before opening Inventory.
Selecting a unit establishes the workspace for your count; it does not demonstrate
a status change or a crew assignment.
In Inventory, the heading identifies Ambulance 61.
The current list shows five training batteries, twenty four nitrile gloves,
and six training oxygen cylinders.
Recent counts appears above that equipment list.
These are fictional software quantities.
On an operational vehicle, first identify the correct supplies and actually inspect
them; the displayed balance is a reference for comparison, not evidence that somebody
has physically counted the equipment.
On the Inventory screen, choose Start count once.
Unit opens a new count for the selected unit and gives it a name
containing the unit and date.
The new record starts In progress, with zero of three counted.
An older completed count remains in history.
This walkthrough follows the new record throughout; it does not create another
count each time the screen is reopened.
On the count screen, read Expected beneath each item.
The light gray five, twenty four, and six inside the fields
are placeholders at this stage.
They are not entered observations: the header still says zero of three counted.
Complete is unavailable until every line has an observation.
Check that header along with the fields, so a screen showing zero differences is
not mistaken for a finished inspection.
Beside the battery field, tap the minus control once.
In this software exercise, that records four against an expected five.
The battery row gains an orange outline, and the header shows one of
three counted with one difference.
This deliberate practice entry is still unsaved.
We do not save or complete the incorrect quantity; the next step corrects it before
any stock adjustment could be posted.
Use the plus control beside the batteries to change four back to five.
The orange outline clears, and the header returns to zero differences.
It still shows only one of three counted because the glove and oxygen
observations have not been entered.
This distinction matters: matching one item does not
complete the rest of the count.
Review both the observation and the progress total after a correction.
For the fictional glove and oxygen quantities, choose Matches
on each corresponding row.
Those controls record the expected twenty four and six as observations.
In service, use Matches only after you have actually checked that the equipment
agrees with the expected balance.
Here the fields now contain five, twenty four, and six, and the header shows three
of three counted with zero differences.
On the count screen, choose Save progress.
The record remains In progress; saving observations does not
itself finalize the count.
The screen still shows the observations, and there is no
pictured success banner to rely on.
Verify persistence through the ordinary history and reopen sequence next.
Keep completion as a separate decision after reviewing the
unit, every observation, and the remaining differences.
Use the back arrow to return to Inventory.
Recent counts now shows two entries with the same unit and date in their titles.
The newer record is In progress, while the earlier record is Completed.
Compare the displayed status and timestamp rather than choosing by title alone.
Open the newer In progress entry to continue the same count you
just saved, while leaving the older completed record unchanged.
The reopened record still shows In progress, three of three
counted, and zero differences.
Read the observations again: five batteries, twenty four
gloves, and six oxygen cylinders.
This is the saved count from the preceding steps.
Reopening provides a useful review before finalization, particularly
on a shared device where another crew may later read the record.
Confirm the selected unit and each line before choosing Complete.
On this reviewed count screen, choose Complete.
The actual iPad confirmation asks Complete count and states that
everything matches what was expected.
It presents Cancel and Complete as separate choices.
Review that message before deciding.
For this authorized zero difference training example, choose
Complete in the confirmation.
That button submits the operation; the next application screen must
establish whether the count actually completed or returned an error.
The result shows Completed and Count completed, with the
saved quantities disabled.
Inventory history now shows both records Completed, and stock
remains five, twenty four, and six.
Reopening the newer count still shows the completed result.
The same review fits community care kits, search and rescue caches, security
patrol supplies, wildland equipment, and industrial protective equipment.
Each team should count what its own assigned unit actually carries
and verify the final record.
